candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics (PAY dataset, key indicators)
candidates.why_relevant: Current harmonised ECB payments-statistics dataset (post-Regulation (EU) 2020/2011) covering all EU/EEA reporting countries including Czechia: card payments, credit transfers, direct debits, e-money, POS terminals, ATMs, semi-annual and quarterly. Machine-readable, English metadata, cross-country comparable — the backbone series for CZ card/POS/ATM benchmarking.
candidates.legal_status: public sector information, ECB reuse policy with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: ECB Data Portal SDMX 2.1 REST API (https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/data/PAY/...) with CSV/SDMX-ML output; snapshot series keys filtered on REF_AREA=CZ; schedule after each semi-annual release
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + ECB Data Portal navigation
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Czechia card payments POS terminals dataset PSS

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments and Settlement Systems Statistics (PSS, discontinued legacy series)
candidates.why_relevant: Legacy harmonised series (annual, from 2000) on access/usage of payment services, payment terminals and national retail/large-value systems; search result indicated ~3,401 Czech Republic series. Essential for LONG time series before the 2022 methodology change and for identifying the definitional break between PSS and PAY.
candidates.access_status: API-only (portal UI states dataset not browsable, API accessible)
candidates.legal_status: public sector information, ECB reuse policy
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off bulk pull via ECB Data Portal API plus the downloadable series-catalogue CSV; archive locally since the dataset is discontinued
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Czechia card payments POS terminals dataset PSS

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payment card accepting devices (data category)
candidates.why_relevant: Category landing page enumerating the exact terminal/POS/ATM series keys (terminals provided by resident PSPs, e-funds transfer POS, ATMs) — the fastest route to the correct series identifiers for CZ terminal-estate tracking, which is the core Printec-relevant indicator family.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape/record series keys once, then pull values via SDMX API
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Czechia card payments POS terminals dataset PSS

candidates.source_name: ECB Payments statistics press releases (semi-annual, e.g. first half of 2025)
candidates.why_relevant: Release-calendar anchor and narrative interpretation of each new payments-statistics vintage; flags revisions, breaks and country-level outliers. Gives the exact publication timing to schedule CZ data pulls and provides EU-wide context for CZ card/terminal trends.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor /press/stats/paysec/ index + RSS; fetch HTML each release
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Czechia card payments POS terminals dataset PSS

candidates.source_name: ECB Statistics portal — Czech-language landing page (Statistiky)
candidates.why_relevant: Confirms ECB publishes statistical navigation in Czech; useful as a local-language entry point and for the official Czech terminology ECB itself uses (statistika platebního styku), which improves cs-language search recall for supranational material.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual reference; harvest Czech terminology for glossary
queries_used: "platebního styku" statistika ECB Česko srovnání evropská statistika platebních karet

candidates.source_name: ČNB — Komentář ke statistice platebního styku (methodological commentary on ECB-regulated reporting)
candidates.why_relevant: Although national, this page is the authoritative bridge document explaining how CZ data is compiled under ECB Regulation (EU) 2020/2011 and fed to the ECB — indispensable for interpreting the supranational CZ series, its breaks from 2022, and the reporting templates (e.g. PSSIVYC22). Reveals why ECB and ČNB figures may differ.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML fetch; diff against previous version to detect methodology changes
candidates.discovered_via_method: Czech-language search (snowball from ECB regulation reference)
queries_used: "platebního styku" statistika ECB Česko srovnání evropská statistika platebních karet

candidates.source_name: EBA/ECB Joint Report on Payment Fraud (annual, PSD2 Art. 96(6) data)
candidates.why_relevant: Only harmonised EU-wide, country-broken-down source on payment fraud by instrument (cards, credit transfers, direct debits, cash withdrawals, e-money), semi-annual, incl. Czechia. Search results indicate CZ appears with above-average per-capita card and credit-transfer fraud losses — high strategic value for security/terminal positioning.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF + annex download; parse country tables; cross-link to ECB payments fraud data in the ECB Data Portal
queries_used: EBA payment fraud report PSD2 data Czech Republic EBA credit institutions register payment institutions

candidates.source_name: EBA Register of payment and electronic money institutions under PSD2 (PIR)
candidates.why_relevant: Daily-updated, machine-readable central register of authorised PIs/EMIs/agents per member state, incl. CZ entities and passporting. Structural actor map of the CZ payments market (acquirers, PSPs, e-money issuers) with change history — a proxy for market entry/exit that no statistical series gives.
candidates.legal_status: public register; EBA notes it is based on NCA-supplied data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled download of the full machine-readable register file, filter country=CZ, snapshot-diff monthly to detect entrants/exits
queries_used: EBA credit institutions register Euclid payment institutions register download

candidates.source_name: EBA Credit Institutions Register (CIR) and other lists of institutions (EUCLID)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative EU-wide list of authorised credit institutions incl. Czech banks and branches, sourced through EUCLID. Provides the denominator/actor list for CZ banking-sector coverage and lets CZ bank population be tracked consistently against other EU markets.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic bulk file download; filter CZ; diff snapshots
queries_used: EBA credit institutions register Euclid payment institutions register download

candidates.source_name: BIS Data Portal — CPMI payments and FMI (Red Book) statistics
candidates.why_relevant: Global harmonised Red Book statistics on LVPS/RPS/FPS, cards, terminals and cash, downloadable as country/comparative tables and CSV/SDMX. Valuable for placing CZ (once matched via ECB data) into a global rather than merely EU frame; note CZ is not a current CPMI member jurisdiction, so its role here is comparator-benchmarking rather than direct CZ coverage.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: BIS Data Portal bulk CSV/SDMX download of CPMI_FMI dataflows; annual refresh
queries_used: BIS CPMI Red Book statistics Czech Republic payment systems tables

candidates.source_name: BIS Data Portal — CPMI CT: retail payments, currency and related indicators (cash trends)
candidates.why_relevant: Banknotes and coins in circulation, narrow money and retail payment indicators in comparable form — the standard reference for cash-usage trend analysis and cash-vs-card substitution narratives. Directly serves the 'cash usage' topic for benchmarking CZ against CPMI peers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX/CSV pull of WS_CPMI_MACRO and CPMI_CT2 publication tables
queries_used: BIS data portal CPMI CT cash trends banknotes in circulation country coverage non-CPMI

candidates.source_name: BIS CPMI — 'Payment systems in the Czech Republic' (Red Book country study, d25)
candidates.why_relevant: Dedicated BIS Red Book country monograph on the Czech payment system — the deepest supranational structural description of CZ clearing/settlement ever published by BIS. Historic (first CZ edition), so use as a baseline/definitional reference and for institutional lineage, not current figures.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off PDF archive
queries_used: BIS CPMI Red Book statistics Czech Republic payment systems tables

candidates.source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual supply-side financial-access indicators normalised per 100,000 adults / per 1,000 km² — ATMs, branches, POS terminals, card and mobile-money transactions — with Czechia reported. The canonical normalised ATM/branch density series for cross-country comparison, with longer and more stable definitions than national releases.
candidates.access_status: open (registration-free; portal migrated to data.imf.org, API endpoints changed)
candidates.legal_status: IMF data terms, attribution, redistribution restrictions on bulk republication
candidates.suggested_collection_method: IMF Data SDMX/JSON API for dataset FAS, indicator subset, REF_AREA=CZE; annual refresh after the autumn release
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey Czech Republic ATMs per 100,000 adults data.imf.org FAS

candidates.source_name: DBnomics mirror of IMF/FAS
candidates.why_relevant: Third-party open mirror of the IMF FAS series with a stable, well-documented API and series browser. Practical fallback when the IMF portal migration breaks endpoints, and convenient for discovering exact FAS series codes for Czechia.
candidates.legal_status: mirror of IMF data; original IMF terms govern reuse
candidates.suggested_collection_method: DBnomics REST/JSON API; treat as secondary, always reconcile against IMF primary
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey Czech Republic ATMs per 100,000 adults data.imf.org FAS

candidates.source_name: FRED (St. Louis Fed) — IMF FAS-derived Czech Republic series
candidates.why_relevant: FRED republishes IMF FAS geographical-outreach and use-of-financial-services indicators as clean per-country time series (e.g. CZ commercial-bank branches, outstanding loans). Excellent low-friction API for charting and vintage tracking of CZ access indicators.
candidates.legal_status: FRED terms; underlying IMF copyright applies
candidates.suggested_collection_method: FRED API series/observations with the CZE* FAS series ids
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey Czech Republic ATMs per 100,000 adults data.imf.org FAS

candidates.source_name: World Bank Open Data — ATMs per 100,000 adults (FB.ATM.TOTL.P5) and related WDI indicators
candidates.why_relevant: World Bank WDI re-publication of the IMF FAS ATM-density indicator with a very stable public API and full country panel — the easiest route to a consistent CZ ATM-density series with peer countries, and useful for detecting when the underlying FAS value was revised.
candidates.legal_status: CC BY 4.0 for most World Bank datasets; underlying IMF source attribution required
candidates.suggested_collection_method: World Bank Indicators API v2 (country/CZE/indicator/FB.ATM.TOTL.P5?format=json)
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey Czech Republic ATMs per 100,000 adults data.imf.org FAS

candidates.source_name: World Bank Global Findex Database 2025
candidates.why_relevant: The only globally comparable DEMAND-side source: ~300 indicators on account ownership, digital payments, card use, mobile/internet use, digital safety and financial resilience from nationally representative surveys of 141 economies incl. Czechia. Complements supply-side ECB/IMF terminal counts with consumer behaviour, incl. cash-vs-digital substitution.
candidates.access_status: open (indicator files and report free; microdata via catalogue registration)
candidates.legal_status: CC BY 4.0 for report/data per World Bank policy; microdata under Microdata Library terms of use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download country-level indicator Excel/CSV from the download-data page; optionally request CZ microdata from the Microdata Library for custom cuts; refresh per Findex wave (~3-4 yearly)
queries_used: World Bank Global Findex 2025 Czechia account ownership digital payments microdata

candidates.source_name: World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey (GPSS)
candidates.why_relevant: Central-bank-answered global survey combining quantitative and qualitative measures of national payment-system development: infrastructure, legal/regulatory environment, retail instruments (cards and terminals), innovation, remittances and oversight. Gives institutional/regulatory context for CZ that pure statistics cannot, and reveals central-bank self-assessment.
candidates.access_status: open reports; underlying respondent-level data partially restricted
candidates.legal_status: public reports; check reuse terms for datasets
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download GPSS iteration reports (2015/2018/2021+) from documents.worldbank.org; extract CZ rows; monitor for the next wave
queries_used: World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey GPSS retail payments dataset country coverage

candidates.source_name: Eurostat — E-banking and e-commerce dataset (isoc_bde15cbc) and ICT usage collections (isoc_i, isoc_e)
candidates.why_relevant: Harmonised EU survey data on internet banking and online purchasing by individuals and enterprises, with Czechia broken out and regional cuts available. The best supranational proxy for CZ digital-payment adoption behaviour and e-commerce demand driving card/POS volumes. Note isoc_bde15cbc itself is a legacy collection (last update 2019); current equivalents live in the isoc_i family.
candidates.legal_status: Eurostat reuse policy — free reuse with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Eurostat SDMX 2.1 / dissemination REST API (statistics/1.0/data/<dataset>?geo=CZ) with annual refresh; also pull the ESMS metadata pages for definitional breaks
queries_used: Eurostat database Czechia financial services indicators ICT usage internet banking isoc_bde15cbc

candidates.source_name: ČSÚ — Mezinárodní data / Publikace obsahující mezinárodní srovnání (Czech NSI gateway to Eurostat & international databases)
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech statistical office's own curated index of the international databases it feeds and links to, in Czech. Snowball hub for discovering which supranational datasets carry CZ data and under what Czech-language labels — closes the cs-language gap around otherwise English-only supranational layers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the index pages for outbound links to Eurostat/OECD/UN datasets; quarterly re-crawl
queries_used: "Eurostat" databáze Česko bankomaty platební karty statistika ČSÚ mezinárodní srovnání

candidates.source_name: Knihovna VŠE — Přehled zdrojů pro statistiku (academic source guide, CZ)
candidates.why_relevant: Prague University of Economics library guide listing Czech and international statistical sources with Czech-language descriptions. A low-cost snowball hub that surfaces supranational and commercial databases a foreign researcher would otherwise miss, and supplies Czech terminology for further searching.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off crawl of outbound links; manual triage
queries_used: "Eurostat" databáze Česko bankomaty platební karty statistika ČSÚ mezinárodní srovnání

candidates.source_name: ECB Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (SPACE)
candidates.why_relevant: The reference methodology and benchmark for POS cash-vs-card behaviour in Europe. Czechia is NOT covered (euro area only), so its value here is methodological (questionnaire design, definitions of POS/P2P shares) and as a comparator set against which any CZ national cash-usage survey must be read.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download report and Annex B methodology PDFs per wave (roughly biennial)
queries_used: ECB SPACE study payment attitudes euro area coverage non-euro EU countries Czechia cash usage survey

negative_findings.description: The ECB SPACE study (payment attitudes / cash usage at POS) covers euro area member states only — 20 countries in the 2024 wave. No Czech sample.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched for CZ inclusion in SPACE; all results confirm euro-area-only scope, with DE and NL running comparable national surveys. Czechia absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single best European demand-side cash-usage instrument does not cover CZ, so cash-usage evidence for CZ must come from Findex, ČNB, or commercial surveys — and cannot be directly compared to SPACE headline shares without caveats.

negative_findings.description: Czechia is not among the 27 CPMI member jurisdictions whose data populate the current BIS Red Book statistics; the only dedicated CZ Red Book material found is the historic country monograph d25.
negative_findings.result_summary: BIS CPMI pages describe Red Book statistics as covering CPMI member jurisdictions; searches surfaced no current CZ country table in CPMI_FMI or CPMI_CT.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: BIS should be treated as a comparator/benchmark layer for CZ, not a CZ data source. Assuming BIS carries current CZ payment statistics would produce empty or wrong extractions.

negative_findings.description: The ECB PSS (legacy payments and settlement systems) dataset is documented as not browsable through the ECB Data Portal UI — accessible only via the API plus a downloadable series-catalogue CSV.
negative_findings.result_summary: Dataset information page states the dataset is not available via the portal interface and can be accessed only via the ECB Data Portal API.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any UI-based or scraping collection design for long CZ back-series will silently fail; the collector must be API-first and must first ingest the series catalogue to resolve keys.

negative_findings.description: Eurostat dataset isoc_bde15cbc (e-banking and e-commerce) is documented as last updated 31/01/2019 covering 2002-2018.
negative_findings.result_summary: Dataset page metadata shows last update 2019; current equivalents must be located in the isoc_i / isoc_ci dataset families.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pinning a collector to isoc_bde15cbc would produce a frozen series. The correct current Eurostat dataset codes for internet-banking use by individuals still need to be resolved from the isoc_i collection.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching produced essentially no Czech-language supranational statistical sources: cs-language results routed almost entirely to ČNB and ČSÚ national pages rather than to ECB/Eurostat/BIS/IMF/World Bank content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two cs queries returned CNB and CSU pages plus one localised ECB statistics landing page; no Czech-language ECB payments dataset documentation, no Czech BIS/IMF/World Bank material.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The supranational layer for CZ is effectively English-only. Local-language discovery for this cell is best used to find the CZ-side bridge documents (methodology, reporting templates) that explain what is fed upward, not to find the supranational data itself.

negative_findings.description: The IMF FAS entry point could not be pinned to a stable dataset-specific URL from search results; the IMF has migrated its data portal to data.imf.org and older dataservices.imf.org / IMF Data endpoints may be redirected or retired.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned the FAS highlights PDF hosted on data.imf.org and third-party mirrors (DBnomics, FRED, World Bank) rather than a canonical FAS dataset landing URL.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collector design should not hard-code an IMF FAS API path without first probing; DBnomics/World Bank mirrors are recommended fallbacks. This is a hypothesis about endpoint instability, not a claim that any URL is dead.

coverage_gaps.description: Exact ECB Data Portal series keys for Czechia POS terminals, ATMs, card counts and card transaction values were not enumerated in this pass — only the dataset and category level was established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download the PAY and PSS series-catalogue CSVs from the ECB Data Portal, filter REF_AREA=CZ, and register the resolved series keys as first-class sources before any collection run.

coverage_gaps.description: The break between the pre-2022 ECB PSS regime and the post-2022 PAY regime under Regulation (EU) 2020/2011 is known to exist but its concrete effect on CZ terminal and card series has not been characterised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair the ECB PAY/PSS pull with the ČNB Czech-language methodological commentary and the ECB regulation text to build an explicit break table before any multi-year trend claim is made.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-ECB European supranational layers were not exhausted: OECD statistics, the European Commission/DG FISMA PSD2 review evidence base, ESRB, and EU open-data portal (data.europa.eu) mirrors of payments data were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up pass on data.europa.eu, OECD Data Explorer, and DG FISMA PSD2/PSR impact-assessment annexes for CZ-broken-out payments evidence.

coverage_gaps.description: No supranational source found that measures CZ cash usage at point of sale in a harmonised, behaviour-level way (SPACE excludes CZ; BIS excludes CZ; Findex measures account/digital-payment use rather than POS payment shares).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat CZ POS cash share as a national-source-only indicator (ČNB, commercial surveys) and flag the absence explicitly in any comparative deliverable; consider Findex digital-payment indicators as the only comparable proxy.

coverage_gaps.description: Only two Czech-language queries were run within this cell and both resolved to national rather than supranational material; Czech terminology for supranational dataset concepts (e.g. akceptační místa, platební terminály, harmonizovaná statistika) remains only partially mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the cs glossary with terminal/acceptance vocabulary (platební terminál, akceptační místo, bezhotovostní platby, hotovostní platby, výběry z bankomatů) and re-run cs discovery specifically against ČNB/ČSÚ bridge documents that cite ECB/Eurostat datasets.

coverage_gaps.description: Redistribution and licensing terms were inferred rather than read for IMF FAS, BIS and Findex microdata.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch and record the terms-of-use pages for data.imf.org, data.bis.org and the World Bank Microdata Library before any internal or client-facing republication of extracted values.

brief: For Czechia, the supranational statistical layer is dominated by the ECB: the ECB Data Portal's PAY dataset (post-2022, Regulation (EU) 2020/2011) plus the discontinued PSS dataset give the only harmonised, machine-readable, long-run CZ series on cards, terminals, ATMs and payment volumes, accessible via SDMX API and accompanied by semi-annual press releases and an EBA/ECB payment-fraud report with CZ country breakdowns. Normalised access metrics come from the IMF Financial Access Survey (ATMs and branches per 100,000 adults), re-published through World Bank WDI, DBnomics and FRED, while demand-side behaviour comes from the World Bank Global Findex 2025 and, for structural/regulatory context, the World Bank GPSS and the EBA payment-institution and credit-institution registers. Two coverage holes matter strategically: Czechia is outside both the BIS CPMI Red Book jurisdictions and the ECB SPACE cash-attitudes survey, so BIS and SPACE serve only as comparator and methodological benchmarks, and no supranational source measures CZ point-of-sale cash shares. The layer is effectively English-only — Czech-language discovery returns ČNB and ČSÚ bridge documents (notably the ČNB commentary on payment-statistics reporting), which are nonetheless essential for interpreting the 2022 definitional break in the ECB CZ series.
